title: Choose the new look for brickbot.ro
question: A fresh look, as you asked. Every card keeps your pinned items: the BRICKBOT wordmark, the motto, a photo of the students, the Support CTA and the top-10 praise. Only the world around them changes, and each one makes lightning and custom shapes part of how it's built.

options.label: Live Wire Panels
options.lineage: action-comic page layout: splash page, panel gutters, caption boxes, hand-lettered sound effects
options.thesis: The page is cut into comic panels by lightning: every gutter is a bolt, every panel a custom shape, and the team is the hero of the splash page.
options.viewport: Splash page: the Nationals photo fills a big tilted panel, the yellow BRICKBOT wordmark bursts over its top edge like a title, a bolt gutter splits off a yellow caption panel with the motto and the Support button, and a starburst shouts “Top 10 in the world · 2026”.
options.risk: Can read childish to a corporate sponsor if the lettering gets cartoony; it has to stay sharp graphic novel, not kids' comic.

raised.raise: Hierarchy by scale contrast alone: one giant line of lettering per panel, with no decoration competing with it.
Every electric flicker fires on one shared pulse, so the page has one heartbeat instead of scattered effects.
Results get one quiet, ruled stat panel (event · year · result) as the page's hard proof, like a card back.
Shape carries meaning: only panels you can click get the bolt-cut corner.
One module, the brick's stud, sets every gutter width and spacing step.

options.label: Race Livery
options.lineage: motorsport team and driver sites: livery, helmet designs, sponsor placements
options.thesis: BrickBot shown as a race team: yellow livery stripes with bolt-cut ends sweep across the page, and every sponsor slot appears as a spot on the livery.
options.viewport: A yellow livery band sweeps diagonally over the students' photo carrying the wordmark; the motto sits beside a giant outlined race number 15996; “Top 10 in the world, 2026” rides as a podium tag; the Support CTA sits on the band.
options.risk: The familiar route: close to many sports-team and F1 driver sites (landonorris.com included). Very clear, but not surprising.

options.label: Hazard Drop
options.lineage: industrial streetwear: quoted labels, zip-tie tags, hazard stripes
options.thesis: A streetwear drop for a robotics team: black-and-yellow high-voltage hazard stripes as structure, literal labels in quotes, zip-tie tags on whatever is active.
options.viewport: Full-bleed student photo under a diagonal hazard band; the wordmark on a stencilled plate; the motto set huge in quotes; “TOP 10 IN THE WORLD” as a quoted label; the Support CTA wears the zip tie.
options.case: Fuses well: black and yellow hazard is literally the electrical warning, and the literal labels make the page very clear. Loses on audience: national sponsors may read it as fashion irony.
options.risk: Streetwear irony can feel try-hard or dated (peak 2018).

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: A giant glyph grid whose weight you drag live.
options.viewport: One giant letter morphing under a slider.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a type-foundry tool says nothing about a robotics team to a sponsor.

options.label: Step Sequencer
options.thesis: Sixteen candy keys under a running chase light.
options.viewport: A step row running across the hero.
options.case: Fun, but a music instrument is foreign to both sponsors and robotics.
options.kept: All motion locked to one shared pulse.

options.label: Wax Pack Cards
options.thesis: The team dealt as collectible cards with stat backs.
options.viewport: A dealt stack of portrait cards.
options.case: Fun, but baseball cards mean little in Romania, and it splits the team into individuals.
options.risk: Nostalgia for a sport nobody here follows.
options.kept: A ruled stat panel as the hard proof.

options.label: Dance Score
options.thesis: A vertical staff where shape encodes motion.
options.case: Too abstract: the kind of conceptual direction you already ruled out.

options.label: Build Instructions
options.thesis: Numbered exploded steps on a stud grid.
options.case: You passed on this route in an earlier round, and sky blue fights the brand.
options.kept: One stud module sets every spacing step.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark team site played straight: full-bleed photo, headline, two buttons, a stats row, then cards.
canonCard.viewport: Photo hero with the motto, two buttons and a stats row underneath.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other team site, by design.
